guides.wedding-hashtag-generator.title: Wedding Hashtags: How to Pick One People Use
guides.wedding-hashtag-generator.desc: A wedding hashtag works when it is short, unambiguous and easy to spell aloud. Here is how to test one before printing it on anything.
guides.wedding-hashtag-generator.lead: The best hashtag is the one a guest can spell correctly after hearing it once. Clever puns fail that test more often than simple name combinations.
guides.wedding-hashtag-generator.f1v: Keep it under 20 characters where possible
guides.wedding-hashtag-generator.f2v: CamelCase each word so it stays readable
guides.wedding-hashtag-generator.f3v: Search the tag before printing — many are already in use
guides.wedding-hashtag-generator.f4v: Use a single official tag, not three similar ones
guides.wedding-hashtag-generator.s1: Combine a shared surname, first-name initials or a short word with the year, then read it aloud to someone who has not heard it. Watch for accidental words hidden inside the joined string, ambiguous letter pairs and numbers that could be a year or an initial. Once chosen, put it in one place guests will actually see — the invitation, the wedding website and a sign at the reception.
guides.wedding-hashtag-generator.s2: Hashtags are most common at US and UK weddings where guests post to public social platforms. In countries where guests use private messaging apps or where wedding photos are kept off public platforms, a shared album or QR code gets better uptake. For multilingual families, avoid wordplay that only works in one language and check that the combined string is not awkward in the other language.
guides.wedding-hashtag-generator.s3: Do not print a tag before searching it on the platforms you care about; an existing event with the same tag will mix your photos into someone else's. Avoid punctuation — hashtags break at spaces and most symbols — and do not assume capitalisation changes the tag, since it usually does not. If guests must remember anything, make it one short string.
guides.wedding-hashtag-generator.q1: Should a wedding hashtag include the year?
guides.wedding-hashtag-generator.a1: It helps if the tag is otherwise common, but it dates the tag and adds characters. Check what is already in use before deciding.
guides.wedding-hashtag-generator.a2: Not for matching — most platforms treat the tag case-insensitively — but CamelCase makes it much easier for guests to read and spell.
guides.wedding-hashtag-generator.q3: What if our surname is hard to spell?
guides.wedding-hashtag-generator.a3: Use first names or initials, and test it by saying it aloud to someone unfamiliar with the name. Prioritise clarity over the pun.
